output: Scientific Hypothesis: The principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) may not be significantly different from the subsequent time horizons (1000 to 500 BCE), as indicated by the mean principal component value of PC1 for the subsequent time horizons (1000 to 500 BCE) being 2.921143 with a standard deviation of 2.188378. However, due to the limited data points and the presence of many missing values, further analysis with more data points would be needed to confirm this hypothesis. The context of the hypothesis is the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE). The variables chosen are the principal component value of PC1 for the beginning of the period (1100 BCE) and the subsequent time horizons (1000 to 500 BCE). The relationship between these variables is that the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period may not be significantly different from the subsequent time horizons, but this needs to be confirmed with more data points. The statistical significance of this relationship is not clear due to the limited data points and the presence of many missing values.
